papers.title: Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results
papers.abstract: The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO) is a satellite experiment of JUNO, designed to measure the reactor antineutrino energy spectrum with high precision at a baseline of 43.2~m from a reactor core using a 2.8-ton spherical liquid-scintillator detector, 1.8~m in diameter, operated at -50 degree and instrumented with 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. The TAO detector installation was completed in 2025, and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. This paper reports the detector design, calibration strategy, and performance based on commissioning data and the first physics runs. Stable cryogenic operation has been achieved, and about 90\% of the readout channels are retained for physics analysis after channel-quality selections. The detector light yield is measured to be about 4000~photoelectrons/MeV after correction for dark noise and optical crosstalk, using neutron capture on hydrogen in inverse beta decay (IBD) events. The energy resolution is about 2.8\% for \(^{68}\)Ge at the detector center and about 3.7\% for \(^{137}\)Cs at \(R=193\)~mm. This energy-resolution performance is among the best reported for reactor-antineutrino detectors and enables TAO to measure the reactor antineutrino spectrum with high precision. Within the fiducial volume of \(R < 800\)~mm, the vertex reconstruction bias remains within \(\pm 30~\mathrm{mm}\), and the resolution is approximately \(70~\mathrm{mm}\) over most of the fiducial volume. The combined muon-tagging efficiency of the veto system is about 97\%. Using 31.3 days of reactor-on data and 29.4 days of reactor-off data, a significant excess of IBD candidates is observed in the reactor-on sample relative to the reactor-off sample, with candidate rates of 2900$\pm$10 events/day and 419$\pm$4 events/day, respectively. The results demonstrate that TAO has reached a high performance level in reactor antineutrino measurement.
papers.reason: Presents commissioning performance and first physics results from the JUNO-TAO reactor antineutrino detector, of supreme interest for precision reactor spectra and oscillation systematics.

summary.tldr: JUNO-TAO reports its commissioning and first physics data, achieving an energy resolution of $2.8\%$ at $1\text{ MeV}$ and measuring an IBD candidate rate of $2900\pm 10\text{ events/day}$.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first operational and physics data from the Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO), a satellite experiment of JUNO utilizing a 2.8-ton cryogenic ($-50^{\circ}\text{C}$) Gd-doped liquid scintillator detector with SiPM readout. It provides an unprecedented light yield ($\,\approx 4000\text{ PE/MeV}$) and energy resolution to measure the unoscillated reactor antineutrino spectrum with minimal model dependence, establishing a benchmark to eliminate flux-shape systematics for JUNO's mass ordering measurement.
summary.method: Data was collected with 4,024 SiPM tiles (8,048 readout channels) over 31.3 days of reactor-on and 29.4 days of reactor-off periods at a 43.2 m baseline. Reconstructed prompt IBD positron energy and vertices were calibrated using central $^{68}\text{Ge}$ and off-center $^{137}\text{Cs}$ sources alongside mono-energetic environmental backgrounds. A data-driven reactor-off subtraction was applied to isolate the IBD positron spectrum while accounting for energy non-linearity, Cherenkov contributions, and boundary leakage.
key_results: Measured a light yield of $\sim 4000\text{ PE/MeV}$ from hydrogen neutron captures in IBD and an energy resolution of $\sim 2.8\%$ for $^{68}\text{Ge}$ at the center and $3.7\%$ for $^{137}\text{Cs}$ at $R=193\text{ mm}$.
Demonstrated stable cryogenic operation at $-50^{\circ}\text{C}$ with temperature variations $<0.2^{\circ}\text{C}$ and retained $\sim 90\%$ of readout channels after quality cuts.
Measured an IBD candidate rate of $2900\pm 10\text{ events/day}$ (reactor-on) versus a cosmogenic/background rate of $419\pm 4\text{ events/day}$ (reactor-off).
Achieved vertex reconstruction bias within $\pm 30\text{ mm}$ and spatial resolution of $\sim 70\text{ mm}$ across the $R < 800\text{ mm}$ fiducial volume.
summary.why_it_matters: TAO's high-resolution reference spectrum is essential for eliminating nuclear summation and flux-shape model uncertainties in JUNO's mass ordering determination, and provides a clean experimental benchmark for testing reactor flux anomalies and sterile neutrino oscillations.
summary.caveats: About 10% of readout channels were inactive during this run, and energy-scale non-linearity parameters currently rely solely on gamma-ray calibration without beta-spectrum constraints from cosmogenic $^{12}\text{B}$.

papers.title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_\pi \approx 200$ MeV and $M_\pi \approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1\sigma$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_\pi \approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.
papers.reason: Presents a state-of-the-art lattice-QCD determination of two-nucleon scattering amplitudes and phase shifts at physical-like pion masses using advanced quantization conditions, directly informing ab initio nuclear responses.

summary.tldr: The BaSc Collaboration extracts nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at near-physical pion masses down to $M_\pi \approx 200\text{ MeV}$ from lattice QCD, explicitly accounting for the one-pion exchange left-hand cut.
summary.novel_idea: Pushes lattice QCD nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) scattering determinations to near-physical quark masses ($M_\pi \approx 200\text{ MeV}$ and $280\text{ MeV}$) using distillation. Crucially, it resolves the proximity of the one-pion exchange left-hand cut by employing two modern formalisms—the plane-wave quantization condition (PWQC) and the relativistic left-hand-cut (LHC) formalism—overcoming the breakdown of standard Lüscher quantization.
summary.method: The calculation uses two $N_f=2+1$ CLS ensembles with $O(a)$-improved Wilson fermions at $a \approx 0.064\text{ fm}$ (D251 with $M_\pi\approx 280\text{ MeV}$ and J250 with $M_\pi\approx 200\text{ MeV}$). Large Hermitian correlation matrices were constructed using LapH distillation perambulators and an extensive operator basis. The spectra were fitted with Bayesian multi-exponential models, and infinite-volume phase shifts were extracted using PWQC and LHC formalisms.
key_results: Extracted low-energy $NN$ scattering phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and shape parameters for both the deuteron ($I=0$) and dineutron ($I=1$) channels.

Near-threshold virtual-state poles (sheet II) are favored by $>1\sigma$ in both channels at $M_\pi \approx 200\text{ and } 280\text{ MeV}$, with the deuteron pole smoothly approaching the threshold as $M_\pi$ decreases.
Demonstrated monotonic approach of inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta toward empirical physical-point values when combined with earlier $M_\pi \approx 710\text{ MeV}$ data.
Extracted the $NN$ mixing angle and $\beta$-wave in the $I=0$ sector directly through one-pion exchange dynamical coupling.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides ab initio QCD constraints on two-nucleon low-energy constants, crucial for refining chiral effective field theory potentials, two-body meson-exchange currents (2p2h), and nuclear responses implemented in neutrino event generators (Achilles, NuWro, GENIE).
summary.caveats: Simulations were performed at a single lattice spacing ($a \approx 0.064\text{ fm}$), leaving discretization systematics unquantified, and the extracted $g_{\pi NN}$ exhibits non-negligible model dependence.

papers.title: Neural Network Representation of Generalized Parton Distributions (NNGPD)
papers.abstract: Extracting generalized parton distributions (GPDs) from experimental observables, the convolution structures denoted as Compton form factors (CFFs), requires solving an intrinsic inverse problem. We presented results using NNGPD, a flexible regression method based on a physics-informed neural-network framework, for reconstructing GPDs using integral constraints -- including CFFs and Mellin moments -- and symmetry and endpoint constraints. The approach does not require pointwise training information on the underlying GPDs. Closure tests using pseudodata generated from a phenomenological model demonstrate the ability of the framework to reproduce the principal features of the underlying distributions across a range of kinematics. A Bayesian neural-network formulation is also introduced to address uncertainties associated with the reconstruction. Finally, we discussed a broader question in GPD phenomenology: whether the complete momentum-fraction dependence of GPDs is necessary to extract physical quantities such as partonic angular momentum. This motivates investigating approaches that infer Mellin moments directly from experimentally constrained CFFs, while quantifying the remaining ambiguities.
papers.reason: Applies a physics-informed neural network framework (NNGPD) to reconstruct generalized parton distributions and Compton form factors from integral constraints.

summary.tldr: The authors introduce NNGPD, a physics-informed neural network framework that reconstructs Generalized Parton Distributions from integral observables like Compton form factors and Mellin moments without pointwise $x$-space training.
summary.novel_idea: Formulates GPD reconstruction as an ill-posed inverse problem tackled via a physics-informed neural network that trains purely on integral constraints—Compton form factors (CFFs) and Mellin moments—along with endpoint conditions and charge-conjugation symmetries. It also introduces a Bayesian neural network (BNN) formulation to quantify reconstruction ambiguities originating from mathematically degenerate 'shadow GPDs'.
summary.method: A neural network parameterizes the GPDs $H_q^+(x,\xi,t)$ and $H_q^-(x,\xi,t)$, whose loss function directly evaluates numerical integrations corresponding to LO/leading-twist CFFs and lower Mellin moments constrained by elastic form factors and lattice QCD. Closure tests were executed on pseudodata generated from a phenomenological spectator model. Variational inference was implemented via a BNN with Kullback-Leibler divergence regularization to sample the posterior distribution of GPDs.
key_results: Demonstrated successful closure on spectator model pseudodata, reproducing both valence $H_{u_v}$ and sea $H_{\bar{u}}$ distributions across varying $x$, $\xi$, and $t$.
Showed that incorporating $n=1$ and higher Mellin moments effectively restricts the space of admissible solutions against CFF shadow ambiguities.
Formulated a direct-inference strategy exploring whether Mellin moments (e.g., for partonic angular momentum) can be reliably extracted from CFFs without resolving full $x$-dependence.
summary.why_it_matters: Co-authored by favorite author S. Pandey; provides advanced physics-informed ML methodology for nucleon structure and hadron matrix elements, bridging experimental scattering with lattice QCD moment constraints.
summary.caveats: The framework has currently only been validated on synthetic closure tests from a spectator model rather than real experimental DVCS cross-section data, and LO QCD approximations were assumed.

papers.title: A REST-based Monte Carlo Simulation and Data Analysis Framework for the N$\nu$DEx Experiment
papers.abstract:
The N$
u$DEx experiment is designed to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0
u eta eta$) of $\mathrm{^{82}Se}$ and is planned to be deployed at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL). It employs a high-pressure time projection chamber (TPC) filled with $\mathrm{^{82}SeF_6}$ gas and a Topmetal pixelated charge readout system. The high $Q_{ eta eta}$ value of $\mathrm{^{82}Se}$, together with the track reconstruction capability of a gaseous TPC, provides strong potential for background suppression. In this work, we develop a full simulation and reconstruction framework for the N$
u$DEx experiment based on the REST (Rare Event Searches Toolkit) software framework. To meet the detector-specific requirements of N$
u$DEx, customized simulation processes are implemented to describe the detector geometry, electron drift and diffusion, the Topmetal readout plane, signal formation, and electronics response. These developments enable a complete software description of the detector response from energy deposition to digitized waveforms. A waveform-fitting-based reconstruction method is further applied to the simulated signals to extract the deposited charge and reconstruct the event energy. For simulated signal events, the reconstructed energy resolution reaches a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of less than 1\%, satisfying the design requirement of the experiment. The resulting simulation and reconstruction chain provides a basis for future studies of detector response, background rejection, event classification, and optimization of the N$
u$DEx detector design.
papers.reason: Develops a REST-based Monte Carlo and reconstruction framework for the NnuDEx high-pressure Se-82 gas TPC for neutrinoless double-beta decay, directly aligned with core rare-event detector workflows.

summary.tldr: A simulation and reconstruction framework based on the REST toolkit is developed for the N$\nu$DEx-100 high-pressure gaseous $^{82}\text{SeF}_6$ TPC searching for $0\nu\beta\beta$.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first complete end-to-end simulation framework for the N$\nu$DEx experiment, incorporating the negative-ion drift dynamics of electronegative $\text{SeF}_6$ gas and direct charge collection via Topmetal-S CMOS sensors without gas avalanche amplification. It exploits the dual-species drift velocity difference ($\text{SeF}_5^-$ and $\text{SeF}_6^-$) to extract $z$-drift coordinate information from waveform fitting.
summary.method: Primary $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay events ($Q_{\beta\beta} = 2.996\text{ MeV}$) were generated using Decay0 and transported in Geant4 within the N$\nu$DEx-100 geometry. REST event processes simulated charge generation ($W = 32\text{ eV}, F = 0.19$), negative-ion mobility and longitudinal/transverse diffusion, and Topmetal-S electronics response. A double-Gaussian convolved with an RC circuit response was fitted to reconstructed waveforms to determine drift distance and energy.
key_results: Optimized waveform fitting parameters with a $5\sigma_{\text{noise}}$ ($225\,e^-$) amplitude threshold and a $50\text{ Hz}$ low-pass filter.
Reconstructed 3D track topologies from 8,192 simulated hexagonal readout channels across 32 modules.
Achieved an energy resolution of $0.58\%$ FWHM ($116/100\ \chi^2/\text{ndf}$) at $Q_{\beta\beta}$, satisfying the experiment's target design requirement ($<1\%$ FWHM).
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates technical modeling of negative-ion transport and pixelated direct charge readout in gaseous TPCs, relevant to rare-event and low-energy neutrino instrumentation.
summary.caveats: The readout plane uses an idealized hexagonal cell approximation rather than full sensor-level electric field focusing, and non-uniform electric field distortions or full radiogenic backgrounds are not yet implemented.

papers.title: Neutrino Anomalies and Tensions: Experimental Status and Theoretical Interpretations
papers.abstract: Neutrino oscillations successfully describe flavor conversion across a wide range of experiments, yet the origin of several excesses and deficits remains unresolved. This review connects these observations and long-baseline parameter tensions to their proposed physical explanations, clarifying what remains open and how it can be tested. We examine reactor and gallium measurements, accelerator appearance and disappearance searches, and atmospheric constraints, focusing on sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and decoherence in open-system dynamics. For each mechanism, we assess what it modifies, which observations it can address, and which theoretical assumptions and independent constraints limit its viability. Recent results have restricted several interpretations and weakened some earlier tensions; no single extension provides an uncontested account of all observations. We identify the flavor, baseline, energy, and event-topology signatures needed to distinguish competing explanations and assess whether the remaining anomalies require new physics or reflect unresolved flux, interaction, and detector uncertainties.
papers.reason: Comprehensive review of neutrino oscillations, short-baseline anomalies, sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and open-system decoherence, highly relevant to experimental phenomenology.

summary.tldr: This review synthesizes experimental neutrino anomalies and parameter tensions, systematically contrasting interpretations including $3+1$ steriles, non-standard interactions, decoherence, and decay across complementary channels.
summary.novel_idea: Provides a structured multi-observable assessment highlighting why single BSM mechanisms struggle to simultaneously explain short-baseline excesses (LSND, MiniBooNE), rate deficits (Gallium/BEST, reactor anomaly), and long-baseline differences (T2K vs NOvA). It emphasizes the critical role of correlated appearance-versus-disappearance limits, nuclear cross-section and flux modeling, and event topology discrimination.
summary.method: Surveys global experimental data across SBL accelerators, reactors, radioactive sources, atmospheric neutrinos (IceCube), and LBL accelerators. Theoretical frameworks—including $3+1$ unitary mixing, vector CC/NC non-standard interactions, open-system Lindblad master equations, neutrino decay, and dark-sector upscattering—are formulated and mapped against experimental signatures ($L/E_\nu$ scaling, energy dependence, NC/CC ratios).
key_results: Reiterates the severe tension in $3+1$ sterile fits between required appearance ($\\sin^2 2\theta_{\mu e} = 4|U_{e4}|^2|U_{\mu 4}|^2$) and null $\nu_\mu$ disappearance results from MINOS+, IceCube, and recent ICARUS data.

Highlights MicroBooNE's exclusion of single-sterile explanations for LSND at $99\%$ CL and MiniBooNE at $95\%$ CL, pointing toward dark-sector upscattering ($e^+e^-$/single photon) or interaction mismodelling.
Notes that Daya Bay flux measurements and updated beta-decay summation calculations resolve much of the reactor rate deficit, isolating the 5 MeV bump as a nuclear flux artifact.
Emphasizes that the recent joint T2K–NOvA Bayesian analysis yields an inverted-to-normal ordering Bayes factor of 1.3, resolving earlier tensions within standard 3-flavor oscillations.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts SBN (SBND, ICARUS, MicroBooNE) physics interpretation, BSM portal searches at accelerator experiments, and interaction-modelling systematics in long-baseline oscillation analyses (T2K, NOvA, DUNE).
summary.caveats: As a review article, it contains no new global fits or original simulations, and primarily catalogs published tensions and theoretical formulations.

papers.title: A Levinson's theorem for particle form factors
papers.abstract: We present and demonstrate a version of Levinson's theorem especially dedicated to the asymptotic behavior of form factor phases. Indeed, as required by analyticity, form factors are multi-valued complex functions of a square four-momentum defined in the complex plane with a cut along the positive real axis. Their phases evaluated on the upper edge of this cut, i.e., on the time-like region, tend asymptotically to integer multiples of $\pi$ radians. The Levinson's theorem establishes a univocal relation between such multiples and properties of form factors related to the dynamics of the electromagnetic interaction of the corresponding hadrons.
papers.reason: Establishes a version of Levinson's theorem for the asymptotic behavior of hadron form factor phases, directly relevant to nucleon form factors and vector-meson dominance.

summary.tldr: The authors prove a form-factor version of Levinson's theorem, demonstrating that the asymptotic timelike phase is uniquely fixed by the number of zeros and the pQCD power-law falloff.
summary.novel_idea: Levinson's theorem traditionally relates asymptotic scattering phase shifts to the number of bound states. The authors adapt this concept to complex analytic particle form factors with a branch cut along the timelike axis. They prove that the net phase change from threshold to infinity is determined solely by the number of isolated zeros and the integer exponent of the asymptotic space-like power-law falloff predicted by pQCD counting rules.
summary.method: The derivation employs Cauchy's argument principle on a contour in the cut complex $s$-plane avoiding the branch cut $[s_{\mathrm{th}}, \infty)$ and isolated singularities. Schwarz reflection and the Phragmén-Lindelöf theorem are utilized to relate space-like asymptotic behavior to time-like phase asymptotes. The relation is verified using logarithmic dispersion relations with constituent-quark counting rule power-laws $s^{-n}$.
key_results: Derived the form factor Levinson relation: $\delta(\infty) - \delta(s_{\mathrm{th}}) = (n - M)\pi$, where $n$ is the asymptotic power-law index ($G(s) \sim s^{-n}$) and $M$ is the number of zeros.
Showed that dressed gluon propagators generating $s^{-n}$ behavior in pQCD can be effectively interpreted as $n$ timelike poles situated above threshold.
Established that only a zero-free form factor approaching a non-zero constant asymptotically satisfies identical phases at threshold and infinity.
summary.why_it_matters: While purely formal, this identity provides a rigorous analytic constraint on dispersion relations and phase parametrizations used in timelike-to-spacelike analytic continuations. It is conceptually relevant when building dispersive representations of nucleon electromagnetic or axial form factors.
summary.caveats: The proof assumes standard analyticity and asymptotic power-law decay, relying on an effective interpretation where gluon exchanges behave as poles outside the physical contour. Experimental validation of timelike phases at high $s$ remains challenging.

papers.title: Gauge-Covariant Wavelets for Quark-Propagator Sparsening and Distillation in Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We develop a novel gauge-covariant wavelet framework for computing hadronic correlation functions in lattice QCD. Two complementary approaches connect spatial localization and resolution-scale separation to propagator sparsening and distillation. A gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform, based on compactly supported biorthogonal filters, coarse-grains quark propagators and reduces early-time excited-state contamination relative to direct decimation at equal spatial reduction. A second construction applies a resolvent filter of the spatial covariant Laplacian to localized sources, generating a distillation subspace without computing Laplacian eigenpairs. We detail its gauge covariance, smearing profiles, and implementation in exact and stochastic distillation. Spatial localization enables unbiased Hansen-Hurwitz sampling of hadronic contractions, reducing their computational cost substantially. We also examine momentum aliasing induced by fixed coarse grids and the use of random grid shifts to remove unwanted contributions in expectation. Numerical benchmarks of the proposed methods are performed with single hadrons, the I = 2 two-pion system, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons. The extracted energy levels agree very well with full or conventional distillation calculations within statistical uncertainties. We quantify the costs of on-demand basis construction and contractions, demonstrate contraction speedups at comparable statistical precision. These studies establish a practical foundation of wavelet-based propagator compression and operator construction for multi-operator calculations of hadronic and nuclear systems, particularly at larger lattice volumes.
papers.reason: Develops novel gauge-covariant wavelet frameworks and distillation methods for quark propagators in lattice QCD, directly relevant to computing hadronic matrix elements for neutrino interactions.

summary.tldr: A gauge-covariant wavelet framework combines fast wavelet transform sparsening and resolvent-filtered Laplacian distillation to dramatically accelerate lattice-QCD correlation function computations and contractions without full Laplacian eigensolves.
summary.novel_idea: The paper introduces multiresolution analysis directly into lattice-QCD hadronic operator evaluation via two complementary methods. First, a gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform (FWT) with biorthogonal filters sparsens propagators while strongly mitigating excited-state aliasing compared to naive decimation. Second, 'wavelet distillation' applies a resolvent filter of the gauge-covariant spatial Laplacian to coarse-grid sources, bypassing costly Laplacian eigensolves and enabling Hansen-Hurwitz importance-sampled Wick contractions.
summary.method: Calculations are benchmarked on $N_f=2+1+1$ MILC (HISQ sea, Wilson-clover valence, $m_\pi \approx 689$ MeV) and $N_f=3$ CLS ($a \approx 0.098$ fm, $m_\pi \approx 429$ MeV) ensembles. Operators for single hadrons, $I=2$ $\pi\pi$, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons are evaluated using GEVP. Stochastic wavelet distillation uses interlace dilution and Hansen-Hurwitz sink sampling, with random grid shifts to remove coarse-grid momentum aliasing.
key_results: Wavelet distillation basis construction is approximately $5\times$ computationally cheaper than standard Laplacian eigensolves on the tested $24^3$ lattice.

Hansen-Hurwitz importance sampling accelerates nucleon and deuteron Wick contractions by factors of 3.8 and 3.0, respectively, with only a $\sim 5\%$ increase in fitted energy statistical uncertainty.
FWT low-pass filtering heavily suppresses high-momentum aliased states compared to direct decimation across coarsening levels $s=1, 2, 3$.
Extracted energy levels for single hadrons, $I=2$ $\pi\pi$, the deuteron, and boosted nucleons match standard distillation within statistical errors.
summary.why_it_matters: Lattice QCD calculations of nucleon axial form factors and multi-nucleon electroweak matrix elements are critical inputs for neutrino-nucleus interaction modelling in generators like Achilles. This framework drastically lowers the computational barrier for boosted nucleons and two-nucleon systems, paving the way for higher-precision lattice inputs to neutrino physics.
summary.caveats: Coarse-grid spatial anchors induce momentum aliasing that requires stochastic random offsets across configurations to cancel in expectation. The method must still be validated on larger volumes ($L \gtrsim 48$) and at physical pion masses.

papers.title: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
papers.abstract: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $\mu_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $\mu=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.
papers.reason: Computes the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude using scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations, directly relevant to nucleon structure and neutrino-nucleus interactions.

summary.tldr: The leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude is calculated from Poincaré-covariant quark-diquark Faddeev amplitudes, revealing how axial-vector diquarks soften the strong longitudinal momentum asymmetry produced by scalar diquarks.
summary.novel_idea: The work provides the first explicit decomposition of the leading-twist proton PDA into its scalar and axial-vector diquark components using an algebraic perturbation-theory integral representation (PTIR) of the Faddeev wave function. It derives closed-form expressions for both chiral-even and chiral-odd axial-vector diquark PDAs and assesses how each correlation channel shapes the proton light-front momentum distribution.
summary.method: The three-quark bound state is formulated via Poincaré-covariant Faddeev equations projected onto light-front coordinates. Spectral representations inspired by Nakanishi representations model the dressed-quark propagators and diquark Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. The resulting proton PDA at $\mu_0 = 0.51$ GeV is evolved to $\mu = 2.0$ GeV at leading order by projecting onto an orthogonal Jacobi-Gegenbauer polynomial eigenbasis of the Brodsky-Lepage kernel.
key_results: Scalar diquarks alone produce a highly asymmetric PDA with peak momentum at $(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (0.55, 0.20, 0.25)$ and Mellin moments $\langle x_1 \rangle = 0.448$, $\langle x_2 \rangle = 0.276$, $\langle x_3 \rangle = 0.276$.

Including axial-vector diquarks (65% scalar, 35% axial-vector) redistributes momentum, shifting low-energy Mellin moments to $\langle x_1 \rangle = 0.392$, $\langle x_2 \rangle = 0.274$, $\langle x_3 \rangle = 0.334$.

LO QCD evolution to $\mu = 2$ GeV further symmetrizes the distribution toward the conformal limit, yielding evolved moments $\langle x_1 \rangle = 0.366$, $\langle x_2 \rangle = 0.302$, $\langle x_3 \rangle = 0.332$ while preserving a distinct non-perturbative imprint.
summary.why_it_matters: Accurate proton PDAs underpin exclusive hard scattering predictions and high-$Q^2$ nucleon electromagnetic and transition form factors. Understanding diquark-driven momentum distributions provides physical insight into the nucleon wave function, informing form factor models used across intermediate- and high-energy neutrino-nucleon interactions.
summary.caveats: The Faddeev amplitudes rely on an algebraic PTIR model rather than direct numerical solutions of the coupled DSE-Faddeev equations. Omitted higher partial waves and orbital angular momentum may further alter the momentum sharing.

papers.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
papers.abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. We point out a distinct coherent channel when the baryonic component that stores the condensate is superfluid: an effective beta-conversion event between a neutron condensate and normal protons can proceed as an Andreev process, converting a particle-like excitation into a hole-like excitation while adding or removing a Cooper pair from the condensate. The resulting Andreev contribution to beta equilibration is fourth order in the effective conversion vertex, is enhanced by anomalous neutron Green's functions, and is not captured by standard Urca process. We identify the density, temperature, and oscillation-frequency regimes where this channel can dominate viscous damping of neutron-star oscillations and mergers.
papers.reason: Proposes a novel Andreev beta-conversion process affecting bulk viscosity in superfluid neutron-star matter, highly relevant to low-energy nuclear matter and astrophysical neutrino sources.

summary.tldr: In superfluid neutron-star matter, coherent Andreev beta conversion mediated by the neutron condensate yields an unsuppressed $T^8$ weak conductance that dominates bulk viscosity over exponentially suppressed quasiparticle Urca at low temperatures.
summary.novel_idea: The authors identify an Andreev-reflection analogue in nuclear beta equilibration: a normal proton and electron convert into a neutron quasiparticle while transferring a Cooper pair to or from the neutron condensate. Unlike standard direct Urca, which suffers exponential gap suppression $\sim e^{-\Delta_n/T}$, this coherent fourth-order channel is mediated by anomalous neutron Green's functions and remains algebraically active at low temperatures.
summary.method: The process is formulated within the Schwinger-Keldysh nonequilibrium field theory formalism using an effective tunneling Hamiltonian where leptons are integrated into the weak vertex. The net beta conversion rate and corresponding beta conductance $\lambda_A$ are calculated from fourth-order Keldysh perturbation theory. Thermodynamic susceptibilities from an equation of state with realistic symmetry energy are then combined with $\lambda = \lambda_{\mathrm{qp}} + \lambda_A$ to compute dynamic bulk viscosity $\zeta(\omega)$.
key_results: The Andreev beta conductance scales asymptotically as $\lambda_A \propto \Delta_n^2 T^8 / |\xi_*|^3$, in contrast to the exponentially suppressed quasiparticle conductance $\lambda_{\mathrm{qp}} \propto T^3 e^{-E_*/T}$.
At temperatures $T \sim 0.1$ MeV, the Andreev channel surpasses ordinary quasiparticle conversion, dominating beta equilibration.

The resulting low-temperature bulk viscosity scales as $\operatorname{Re}\zeta(\omega) \propto T^8$ rather than freezing out exponentially, directly modifying the viscous damping of neutron-star pulsations and mergers.
summary.why_it_matters: This mechanism alters the dissipation and weak-interaction equilibration rates in cold, dense neutron star matter, directly impacting post-merger gravitational wave damping and neutrino emissivity/cooling. While focused on bulk astrophysical matter rather than terrestrial neutrino detection, it highlights novel condensate-mediated weak transport relevant to dense astrophysical neutrino environments.
summary.caveats: Lepton phase-space and Fermi-liquid renormalizations are absorbed into a phenomenological effective coupling $g_F$. The analysis assumes an isotropic $S$-wave pairing gap; anisotropic $P$-wave pairing with nodes could alter the relative power-law scaling.

papers.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
papers.abstract: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.
papers.reason: Quantifies statistical model uncertainties in neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework, providing essential nuclear physics inputs for supernova and r-process nucleosynthesis.

summary.tldr: Hauser-Feshbach statistical uncertainties in neutron-capture rates, dominated by nuclear level densities rather than gamma-ray strength functions, propagate significantly into r-process abundances, particularly in cold nucleosynthesis regimes.
summary.novel_idea: The study performs a comprehensive sensitivity analysis of r-process nucleosynthesis by propagating 60 statistical model combinations (varying NLDs and GSFs in TALYS-2.0) across 10,000 parametric astrophysical trajectories and full neutron-star merger ejecta. It systematically delineates how the timing of equilibrium freeze-out relative to r-process freeze-out controls nucleosynthetic sensitivity to statistical nuclear inputs.
summary.method: Neutron-capture cross sections and reactivities $\langle \sigma v \rangle$ were computed with TALYS-2.0 using the FRDM2012 mass model and Koning-Delaroche optical potential across 6 NLD and 10 GSF models. Nucleosynthesis evolution was tracked with the WinNet reaction network for a dynamic NSM ejecta trajectory, a disk outflow, mass-integrated NSM ejecta, and a $100\times 100$ grid of $(Y_{e,0}, s_0)$ parametric trajectories.
key_results: Nuclear level densities induce up to an order of magnitude variation in final abundances below $A \approx 130$ and between the rare-earth and third peaks, far outweighing GSF variations (typically under a factor of 2).
Persistent NLD-driven structures survive mass integration in NSM ejecta, notably a subpeak at $A \sim 172-178$ and abundance variations at $A \sim 180-194$.
Sensitivity is strongly enhanced in 'cold r-process' conditions where equilibrium freeze-out precedes neutron exhaustion, allowing post-equilibrium neutron captures to reshape isotopic distributions.
summary.why_it_matters: This work belongs to nuclear astrophysics and heavy-element nucleosynthesis rather than neutrino physics. It is only tangentially related through the electron fraction $Y_e$ set by neutrino interactions in merger ejecta.
summary.caveats: The study keeps the nuclear mass model fixed to FRDM2012, neglecting potential correlated uncertainties between masses and statistical model parameters. Many considered NLD/GSF models are poorly constrained far from stability.

papers.title: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.
papers.reason: Analyzes the impact of irrep truncations and electric bases on quantum simulations of SU(3) lattice gauge theory, aligning with advanced theoretical approaches to QCD gauge dynamics.

papers.title: $N\Lambda$ interaction from a quark model: $p\Lambda$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton
papers.abstract: Understanding the low-energy nucleon--$\Lambda$ interaction is essential for describing hypernuclear structures, while its spin dependence remains insufficiently constrained by experimental data. In this work, we investigate the $N\Lambda$ interaction using the quark delocalization color screening model and explore its implications for $p\Lambda$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton. The energy and scattering phase shifts of the $N\Lambda$ system are calculated, revealing weak attraction in both the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ channels, but no bound states. The corresponding scattering lengths and effective ranges are found to be $-2.36$ fm and $1.61$ fm for $J^P=0^+$, and $-0.95$ fm and $1.46$ fm for $J^P=1^+$, respectively. Using the Gel'fand--Levitan--Marchenko inverse-scattering method, effective $N\Lambda$ potentials are reconstructed from the coupled-channel scattering phase shifts and applied to calculate the $p\Lambda$ femtoscopic correlation function. Comparison with experimental data suggests that the spin-triplet attraction may be underestimated in the present model. Furthermore, employing the Gaussian Expansion Method, we investigate the $NN\Lambda$ three-body system and obtain a weakly bound hypertriton with a $\Lambda$ separation energy of $1.06$--$1.16$ MeV. These results demonstrate that $p\Lambda$ femtoscopic correlations and hypertriton binding provide complementary probes of the spin-dependent $N\Lambda$ interaction, offering valuable constraints on its low-energy behavior.
papers.reason: Investigates low-energy nucleon-Lambda interactions, p-Lambda femtoscopy, and hypertriton binding using quark models, highly relevant to nuclear interactions and hyperon production.

papers.title: Isovector Monopole Resonance
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical study of the three isospin channels of the isovector giant monopole resonance (IVGMR) within self-consistent Skyrme Hartree-Fock plus Random-Phase Approximation. A modified charge-exchange monopole operator is introduced to remove the dominant isobaric-analog-state contribution, thereby isolating the genuine radial isovector response. We derive the associated non-energy- and energy-weighted sum rules and establish approximate relations between the charge-exchange and non-charge-exchange strengths. The relative locations of the three IVGMR centroids are interpreted in terms of Coulomb displacement energies, the neutron-proton mass difference, and the finite-nucleus symmetry potential. Calculations for \(^{48}\)Ca, \(^{90}\)Zr, and \(^{208}\)Pb show that the non-charge-exchange centroid is accurately approximated by the average of the two charge-exchange centroids in medium-heavy and heavy nuclei. Using a broad set of Skyrme energy-density functionals, we find that the centroid energies of the three channels display a weak model dependence for a fixed nucleus, whereas the non-charge-exchange monopole polarizability exhibits a clear sensitivity to the density dependence of the symmetry energy. These results clarify the isospin structure of the IVGMR and support its use as a complementary probe of isovector nuclear properties.
papers.reason: Theoretical study of the isovector giant monopole resonance and symmetry energy sensitivities using Skyrme functionals, directly relevant to nuclear responses.

papers.title: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
papers.abstract: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CE$\nu$NS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.
papers.reason: Reports improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response for athermal phonon detectors used in Dark Matter and CEvNS experiments.

papers.title: Universal Long-distance Tail of Particle-number Density near a Wall in Superfluids
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-distance recovery of the particle-number density near a static, impermeable wall in a $d$-dimensional Galilean-invariant superfluid. Using superfluid effective field theory (EFT) on a half-space, we show that quantum phonon fluctuations produce a $z^{-(d+1)}$ tail in the smooth density profile at zero temperature, where $z$ is the distance from the wall. The tail coefficient is fixed by the bulk equation of state and is independent of microscopic wall details. At low temperature $T$, the thermal length $c_s/T$, with $c_s$ the bulk sound speed, separates the zero-temperature behavior at intermediate distances from a thermal $Tz^{-d}$ tail at larger distances for $d>1$. For $d=1$, the long-distance phonon contribution instead decays as $\exp(-4\pi Tz/c_s)$. The EFT applies to both Bose and Fermi superfluids, including strongly interacting Fermi gases at unitarity. We estimate the normalized tail amplitude in three dimensions across the BCS--BEC crossover using experimental sound-speed data.
papers.reason: Calculates the particle-number density tail near a wall in superfluids using effective field theory, offering useful methodological parallels for nuclear surface properties.

papers.title: Exploring QCD Matter through Energy Correlators of Soft Hadrons
papers.abstract: We propose energy-energy correlators (EECs) of soft hadrons and their azimuthal harmonics as new soft observables to probe the collective flow and correlations beyond flow for large and small systems created in high energy nuclear collisions. We separate the soft EEC into a disconnected contribution determined by the mean energy flow and a connected contribution encoding correlations beyond it. Viscous hydrodynamic simulations demonstrate that the soft EEC of a fluid system is governed by the disconnected contribution, while its elliptic and triangular harmonics respond to the initial geometry and shear viscosity as traditional flow harmonics do. Comparisons between iEBE-VISHNU and PYTHIA for p+p, O+O, and Pb+Pb collisions show that the disconnected contribution dominates at large angles in all systems, whereas connected correlations beyond the mean energy flow grow toward small angles and small systems, most strongly for the harmonics. Soft EECs thus provide a unique window into collective flow and correlations beyond it across collision systems.
papers.reason: Applies energy-energy correlators of soft hadrons to heavy-ion collisions and small systems, relevant to hadronization and QCD matter.

papers.title: The Singular Structure of Rapidity Distributions for Color-Singlet Production at N3LO
papers.abstract: We determine the universal singular structure of rapidity distributions for color-singlet production in hadron collisions through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in QCD. Our result captures the full singular contributions as either partonic momentum fraction approaches one, including the delta-function terms, while retaining the exact dependence on the other. The essential new ingredient is the complete calculation of the three-loop quark and gluon rapidity beam-function matching kernels. Our calculation is based on the strict collinear expansion of the partonic cross sections for Higgs boson and Drell-Yan production. We represent our results in terms of generalized polylogarithms as well as numerical series expansions. The resulting N3LO partonic coefficient functions apply to arbitrary color-singlet production processes with the process dependence entering through the hard function, which encodes the virtual corrections to the Born process.
papers.reason: Computes universal singular structure and beam-function matching kernels for N3LO rapidity distributions in color-singlet production.

papers.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $\chi_4^Q/\chi_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $\chi_4^Q/\chi_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=\kappa_Q\sigma_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $\kappa_Q$ and $\sigma_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.
papers.reason: Investigates anisotropic hadronic matter, equation of state, and conserved-charge fluctuations in magnetic fields using a hadron resonance gas framework.

papers.title: Effects of kinematic cuts on $v_0(p_T)$
papers.abstract: We show that the analysis of $v_0(p_T)$ is biased when low-$p_T$ particles are not detected. The low-$p_T$ threshold shifts $v_0(p_T)$ by a constant negative value, which depends on the threshold. We evaluate the shift using hydrodynamic simulations. Correcting for this bias significantly improves agreement between ALICE and ATLAS results for $v_0(p_T)$ in Pb+Pb collisions.
papers.reason: Analyzes biases from kinematic cuts on anisotropic flow coefficients v0(pT) in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
papers.abstract: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.
papers.reason: Regularization and non-perturbative renormalization of shear viscosity in stochastic fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.
papers.reason: Completes the O(g^6) weak-coupling pressure calculation for hot Yang-Mills theory using thermal loop-tree duality.

papers.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
papers.abstract: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained in arXiv:1204.6184 by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.
papers.reason: Perturbative determination of the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to gluon plasma pressure at O(g^6).

papers.title: Revisiting the Wess-Zumino-Witten Term in Nuclear and Quark Matter under Magnetic Fields and Rotation
papers.abstract: We study anomalous Wess-Zumino-Witten terms associated with the chiral anomaly in dense QCD matter under magnetic fields and rotation. By introducing electromagnetic, baryon number, and isospin background gauge fields, we write down the topological couplings of neutral mesons for the $N_f=2$ and $N_f=3$ cases. The resulting terms contain characteristic contributions proportional to $\vec{B} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$ and $\vec{\Omega} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$, where $\phi$ denotes $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$. These results are relevant to chiral soliton lattices in dense rotating matter.
papers.reason: Revisits anomalous Wess-Zumino-Witten terms in dense QCD matter under magnetic fields and rotation, relevant to nuclear matter dynamics.

papers.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
papers.abstract: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. A component correlated with a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) annihilation template remains with finer spatial binning and the instrumental response included. Outside the Fermi bubbles footprint, it is detected at nominal significances of about 4-16$\sigma$ over 5.6-130 GeV, falling to 1-7$\sigma$ when the enlarged boundaries of a recent substructured bubbles model are also excluded. With the substructured model, which improves the fit substantially, the component remains at 7-18$\sigma$ in four of six representative foreground configurations. However, its amplitude and spectrum depend strongly on the foreground model, and no tested foreground yields a single NFW normalization across the sky, including with additional spatial freedom in the eROSITA bubbles. Simulations show that foreground mismodeling can produce spurious NFW-correlated emission of the observed amplitude, and that residual-derived bubbles templates can bias the recovered spectrum. The 420 GeV $W^+W^-$ spectrum motivated by the LZ connection describes the data for some foreground models but is disfavored by others. These results disfavor interpreting the full excess as annihilation in a smooth NFW halo and weaken the case for a common origin with the LZ event, but they do not exclude a dark matter contribution to the persistent halo-like residual. [abridged]
papers.reason: Evaluates foreground dependencies in Fermi-LAT data for the 20 GeV Galactic halo excess and its connection to dark matter searches, relevant to astrophysical backgrounds for low-energy and indirect neutrino/dark matter detectors.

papers.title: Unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry in nucleus-nucleus collisions at CERN SPS energies
papers.abstract: The NA61/SHINE experiment at the CERN SPS reports an unexpectedly large excess in the inclusive production of charged over neutral kaons in 0-10% central Ar+Sc collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{{NN}}}=8.8$ and 11.9 GeV. This effect corresponds to an unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry, that cannot be explained by known mechanisms contained in the present theoretical models. The comparison of the NA61/SHINE results to data from other experiments reveals, within sizeable uncertainties, a consistent isospin symmetry-violating excess of charged kaon production in the energy regime $2.6<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<200$ GeV. At LHC energies ($0.9<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<13$ TeV) the charged-over-neutral kaon ratio appears consistent with unity, but the uncertainties remain sizeable. A similar excess of charged over neutral kaon yields is observed by NA61/SHINE in minimum bias $\pi^-$+C reactions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=17.3$ and 25.7 GeV, also in disagreement with model predictions. No clear theoretical explanation of these phenomena has been provided so far. An unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry brings potential heavy consequences for our understanding of particle production, and calls for a concentrated experimental and theoretical effort.
papers.reason: Reports unexpected isospin symmetry violation in charged-to-neutral kaon production in nucleus-nucleus collisions, relevant to secondary beam flux calculations and hadronic interaction models.

papers.title: Long-Lived Charge Trap Characterization for Rare-Event Searches with Skipper-CCDs
papers.abstract: Skipper Charge-Coupled Devices (Skipper-CCDs) are detectors with sub-electron resolution, allowing them to play a critical role in rare-event searches. A major challenge in experiments using these detectors is understanding and mitigating low-energy backgrounds which impact the single-electron rate. One potential component of the single-electron rate could arise from single-electron charge traps caused by lattice defects. In this work we use a new in-situ technique for generating uniform charge known as ``pixel-pumping'' across the CCD to study single-electron traps in a SENSEI sensor placed underground in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab, which enables sensitivity to long-lived traps with emission times $>10^3$ seconds, a regime that was previously not accessible. We fully characterize 1787 traps and use this information to estimate their contribution to the single-electron background in SENSEI. Through simulation, we find the characterized population of traps does not significantly impact the single-electron rate. We further identify the energies and cross-sections for traps to which this analysis is sensitive, and compare this with the values that could impact the single-electron rate. This analysis probes a large fraction of this region. However, we also see that a sufficiently numerous hidden population could contribute significantly to the single-electron rate, and new measurement techniques will have to be devised in order to fully rule out this population.
papers.reason: Characterizes long-lived charge traps in Skipper-CCDs using pixel-pumping to evaluate low-energy backgrounds, relevant to low-threshold direct detection and coherent scattering detectors.

papers.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
papers.abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.
papers.reason: Performs fast simulations of proton-number fluctuations in uranium-uranium collisions at high-baryon-density energies, which is somewhat adjacent to heavy-ion background modeling for neutrino experiments.

papers.title: Observation of the ${\Xi_b^-\to \Xi^-\mu^+\mu^-}$ and study of the ${\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-\psi(2S)}$ decays
papers.abstract: The rare decay ${\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-\mu^+\mu^-}$ is observed for the first time using proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at centre-of-mass energies of $7$, $8$ and~$13~\text{TeV}$, corresponding to integrated luminosities of $1$, $2$ and $6~\text{fb}^{-1}$, respectively. Its branching fraction is reported in intervals of the dimuon invariant mass squared. The integrated value of ${\cal{B}}(\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-\mu^+\mu^-)$ is measured to be ${ (118 \pm 24 \pm 7 \pm 38 ) \times 10^{-8}}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is systematic and the third uncertainty arises from the normalisation branching fraction ${\cal{B}}(\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-J/\psi)$, whose uncertainty is dominated by SU(3)-breaking effects. In addition, the ratio of the branching fractions of the ${\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-\psi(2S)}$ and the ${\Xi_b^-\to\Xi^-J/\psi}$ decays is measured to be ${ 0.491 \pm 0.041 \pm 0.019 }$.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
papers.reason: LHCb measurement of rare Xi_b decays and branching fractions, marginally relevant for flavor/baryon anomalies.

papers.title: Explaining $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ with CKM Unitarity Violation? A No-Go Theorem
papers.abstract: The deficits w.r.t.~the Standard Model predictions in $B\to K^{(*)}\mu^+\mu^-$ and $B_s\to \phi\mu^+\mu^-$ have recently been substantiated by new analyses from LHCb and CMS, as well as improved theoretical predictions, resulting in strong statistical evidence for lepton flavour universal new physics effects. In this letter, we investigate the possibility of generating such an effect through CKM unitarity violation: If the true value of $V_{cb}$, extracted from $B\to D^{(*)}\ell\nu$, were larger due to an NP contamination, this would lead, via the assumed CKM unitarity within the SM, to a smaller value of $V_{ts}$ and thus to reduced theory predictions for $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ branching ratios. A sizable correction to the $W$-$c$-$b$ vertex is only possible close to the custodial-protected limit in which $Z$-$b$-$s$ couplings are absent. However, in a model-independent SMEFT analysis, we show that even if $C_{Hq}^{(1)}=-C_{Hq}^{(3)}$ is realized at a high scale, additional custodial-breaking effects appear due to RGE. Therefore, only a fine-tuned region in the parameter space of modified gauge boson couplings, displaying an overcompensation of the CKM unitarity-violating effect, gives a good fit to $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ data. The only realistic simple SM extensions to achieve this setup are vector-like quarks. However, we show that they cannot explain the $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ anomalies without violating bounds for electroweak precision observables as well as $K^0-\bar K^0$ and $B_s-\bar B_s$ mixing.
papers.topic: b to s l+ l- anomalies
papers.reason: Investigates b to s l+ l- anomalies through CKM unitarity violation in SMEFT, adjacent to BSM lepton flavor physics.

papers.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.
papers.reason: Analyzes entropy production and thermalization for heavy quarks in the QGP via Langevin dynamics.

papers.title: A comparative study of variational quantum classifiers and classical machine learning for $tW-t\bar{t}$ discrimination at the LHC
papers.abstract: Precise measurements of single top-quark production in the associated $tW$-channel require efficient discrimination against the dominant $t\bar{t}$ background. In this work, we investigate the applicability of quantum machine learning to this classification problem using the Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) algorithm. Simulated proton-proton collision events from CMS Open Data corresponding to Run-2 are employed to train and evaluate the VQC model. Its performance is compared with two established classical approaches, Boosted Decision Trees (BDTs) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) using both machine learning metrics and physics-motivated metrics that describe the Signal Significance as a function of Signal Efficiency. The comparison is performed separately for the dileptonic $e-\mu$ channel and for the resolved and boosted hadronic topologies. In addition, signal-enriched and background-enriched phase-space regions are studied to assess the dependence of classifier performance on event topology. Our results provide a systematic benchmark for the application of VQC for a realistic High Energy Physics classification task and identify the analysis regimes wherein quantum-inspired models offer competitive discrimination with respect to established classical techniques.
papers.reason: Compares variational quantum classifiers with BDTs and MLPs for top-quark discrimination at the LHC.

papers.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
papers.abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.
papers.reason: Fermi-LAT constraints on B=1 decaying dark matter and gamma-ray spectra, relevant to dark matter searches.

papers.title: Gauge Interactions Involving New Vector and Pseudoscalar Particles
papers.abstract: The Vector gauge bosons $Z'$ and axion-like particles (ALPs) $a$ are predicted by the $U(1)_X$ gauge extension and Peccei-Quinn (PQ) models, respectively. We focus on the interactions of the $Z'$ boson and the $a$ particle with the $W^\pm$ gauge boson, and investigate the production cross section and related kinematic distributions for the $Z'/a\to W^+W^-$ decay process at hadron colliders. We consider the angular distributions of charged leptons in the final states corresponding to the semileptonic and fully leptonic decays of the $W^\pm$ boson, separately. The study shows that, in the associated production processes of $Z'/a$ with $W^+$ or $Z$ bosons, the angular distributions of final-state leptons can serve as an important observable for probing new gauge interactions, and can also provide a criterion to distinguish vector particles from pseudoscalar particles.
papers.reason: Probing new vector and pseudoscalar gauge interactions via W boson decays and leptonic angular distributions at colliders.

papers.title: About All-Charm Tetraquarks in S and P Waves
papers.abstract: We present a quantitative analysis of masses and decays of $cc \bar c \bar c$ tetraquarks, with diquarks and antidiquarks in S and P wave. We study explicitely the decays of the $4P-J^{PC}=3^{--},~2^{--}$ into 4 muons and into hidden- and open-charm mesons and estimate its width and branching ratios. Based on our results and with the present sensitivity, LHCb, CMS and ATLAS should detect the $4P-J^{PC}=3^{--},~2^{--}$ fully-charmed tetraquark. We note that one decay channel of the $4P-J^{PC}=2^{--}$could lead to the identification of the (still controversial) $\chi_{c1}(2P)$.
papers.reason: Mass and decay analysis of fully-charmed tetraquarks accessible at LHCb and CMS.

papers.title: Search for dark photon in association with charged leptons at electron-positron colliders
papers.abstract: The dark photon can serve as a vector portal between the dark sector and the Standard Model via kinetic mixing. In this paper, we investigate the production of an invisible dark photon via the process $e^+ e^- \to \ell^+ \ell^- A'$ with $\ell=e,\mu$, at the Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC). The production cross sections for the signal process are calculated, and the kinematic distributions for the signal and background processes are analyzed. We further compute the branching ratio for the invisible decay of the dark photon, and explore the discovery potential of dark photons at the CEPC. It is found that dark photons with masses in the range $1~\mathrm{GeV} < M_{A'} < 16~\mathrm{GeV}$ are potentially detectable at the CEPC.
papers.reason: Search for invisible dark photons in association with charged leptons at the CEPC.

papers.title: $\chi_{c1}(4010)$ as a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ Molecular State: Mass, Decay Constant, and Width
papers.abstract: The charmonium-like state $\chi_{c1}(4010)$, recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration in $B^+ \to D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}K^+$ decays, is investigated as an axial-vector $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular state within the QCD sum rule approach. A two-point sum rule incorporating quark, gluon, and mixed vacuum condensates up to dimension $10$ yields the mass and decay constant, $m_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (4005.89 \pm 47.15)~\text{MeV}$ and $f_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (2.87 \pm 0.55)\times 10^{-3}~\text{GeV}^{4}$, in agreement with the LHCb measurement. Since this mass lies above the $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ threshold, the strong coupling constants at the $\chi_{c1}(4010)D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ vertices are extracted from three-point sum rules and used to compute the partial widths of the $D^{*-}D^{+}$ and $D^{*+}D^{-}$ channels. The resulting total width, $\Gamma_{\chi_{c1}(4010)} = (57.64 \pm 9.64)~\text{MeV}$, is compatible with experiment within uncertainties. These results support a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular interpretation of $\chi_{c1}(4010)$ and offer sum-rule predictions for comparison with future measurements at BESIII, LHCb, and Belle~II.
papers.reason: QCD sum rule analysis of the chi_c1(4010) as a D*D molecular state, relevant to exotic hadron spectroscopy.

papers.title: $\psi(3S)$ and $\eta_c(3S)$ production in the $B^+$ decay processes
papers.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the production of psi(4040) in the B+ -> K+ psi(4040) process. Our estimations indicate that the unexpectedly large branching fraction could be well reproduced by taking both the short-range perturbative and long-range non-perturbative QCD contributions into account, where the long-range non-perturbative part plays an important role. Considering the structural similarity of eta_c(3S) and psi(3S), we apply the same model parameters to investigate the production of eta_c(3S) in the B+ decay process, and the branching fraction is predicted to be (0.81 +0.31 -0.29) x 10^-3. Based on the estimations in the present work and the relevant experimental measurements, we suggest that the experimentalists search for eta_c(3S) in the J/psi omega invariant mass distributions of B+ -> J/psi omega K+ process at Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.
papers.reason: Estimates branching fractions for psi(3S) and eta_c(3S) in B decays using perturbative and non-perturbative QCD.

papers.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
papers.abstract: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.
papers.reason: Analyzes hidden sector relic abundances and energy injection from inflation using an effective Planck mass.

papers.title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
papers.abstract: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in the semileptonic final state $b\bar{b}\,\ell\nu q\bar{q}'$ to construct an anomaly detector for non-$t\bar{t}$ events. Wigner $D$ functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-$t\bar{t}$ concentrate at low $t\bar{t}$ density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.
papers.reason: Constructs an anomaly detector using angular distributions and Wigner D functions for top-quark pair final states.

papers.title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
papers.abstract: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades.
